summary: Install-time beacon to hardcoded IP in dependency-confusion squat of react-bootstrap-table2-toolkit
details: Package name resembles the popular `react-bootstrap-table2-toolkit` with a `-bg` suffix and is published at version 9.9.9, a shape typically used to win dependency-confusion resolution against internal packages. On `npm install`, a lifecycle script executes beacon code that collects host identifiers via `os.hostname()`, `os.userInfo()`, `process.cwd()`, and `process.platform` and sends them as query parameters in a plain-HTTP GET to the hardcoded bare IP `http://100.24.177.136/cb`. The destination is not a package registry or publisher-matched endpoint, uses an IP literal rather than a domain, and transmits over cleartext HTTP. The manifest description self-labels the package as an authorized dependency-confusion proof-of-concept; such author-controlled labels do not change the behavior, which exfiltrates installer identity to an attacker-controlled endpoint on every install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
